title: 29-30. DO NOT BURY ME IN EGYPT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When the time drew near for Israel to die, he called for his son Joseph and said to him, 'If I have found favour in your eyes, put your hand under my thigh and promise that you will show me kindness and faithfulness. Do not bury me in Egypt, but when I rest with my fathers, carry me out of Egypt and bury me where they are buried.' 'I will do as you say,' he said." — Gen 47:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob has spent seventeen comfortable years in Egypt. He has land, family, security, and a son who is second only to Pharaoh. And his dying request is: do not bury me here.

He wants to be laid in the cave at Machpelah, where Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, and his own wife Leah lie. Not because the location is magical, but because it is in the land God promised. Even in death, Jacob is staking a claim on God's word.

This is faith. Hebrews lists this family precisely for this reason: they died still believing, admitting they were foreigners on earth and looking for a better country (Heb 11:13-16).

Comfort had not changed Jacob's mind about where he belonged. Seventeen good years in Egypt could not make Egypt home.

That is a searching question for us. Comfort is the most effective thing there is at making us forget we are pilgrims. Nobody drifts away from God during a famine; we drift during good years.

Jacob died holding onto a promise he had not yet seen fulfilled. So can we — ours is fixed in a Saviour who has already risen.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has comfort ever loosened your grip on God's promises?
2. What would it look like to live and die holding onto God's word?
3. Where is your true home, and does your life show it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, do not let comfort make me forget where I belong. Keep me holding onto Your promises to the very end, with my hope fixed on Christ who has already risen. Amen.
